speeches.speaker: Josh Frydenberg
speeches.brief: Introduced the Statute Law Revision Bill (No. 1) 2014, correcting minor technical errors and outdated terminology across Commonwealth legislation, and cited the Melbourne 2006 Commonwealth Games (Indicia and Images) Protection Act 2005, which ceased to have effect on 30 June 2006, as an example of a redundant act being repealed.

speeches.speaker: Mark Dreyfus
speeches.brief: Mocked the statute law revision bill as trivial housekeeping dressed up as reform, citing changes such as replacing the hyphenated 'e-mail' with 'email' and fixing a spelling error in the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Act. Challenged the government to justify its claim that repeal day would save more than $700 million a year by scrapping 9,500 regulations and 1,000 redundant acts.

speeches.speaker: Mark Dreyfus
speeches.brief: Argued the amending acts repeal bill changes nothing, noting the Commonwealth Star's size has been unchanged for 60 years despite the repeal of the amending act. Said the former Labor government repealed 16,794 acts and instruments while delivering real reforms, and warned that unwinding the Future of Financial Advice laws risked a repeat of the Storm Financial collapse.

speeches.speaker: Julie Owens
speeches.brief: Mocked further trivial changes in the repeal bill, noting six pieces of legislation were amended just to add a space making 'trademark' read 'trade mark', and that 10 instances of Northern Territory legislative wording were corrected from 'for' to 'of'.

speeches.speaker: Josh Frydenberg
speeches.brief: Said Telstra will no longer need to provide 70,000 pages of wholesale contracts to the ACCC under the reforms, which deliver a $720 million pay-off by removing more than 10,000 redundant regulations, and noted Australia ranked a lowly 128th out of 148 countries for regulatory burden under Labor.

speeches.speaker: Josh Frydenberg
speeches.brief: Answered questions from the day's repeal debate, citing $0.21 million and $0.35 million in annual compliance savings from two repeal bills, and said the previous government's 21,000 additional regulations left Australia ranked 128th out of 148 countries for regulatory burden.
